items.title: US-backed consortium signs conditional agreement to acquire Lukoil international energy assets
items.summary: An Eldridge-led consortium including the US development finance agency signed an agreement to acquire Lukoil's non-Russian energy assets. The portfolio includes major upstream operations and three European refineries. Separate OFAC authorization is required; no transfer of ownership or incremental physical production has occurred.

observations.label: Agreement announced November 25; independently reported November 26
observations.value: Definitive conditional acquisition agreement; Eldridge, DFC, Catena and Xtellus; restricted-share exchange rather than direct cash payment to Russia.

observations.label: Current upstream scale
observations.value: Approximately 350,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day across 11 countries, per consortium.

observations.label: Refining capacity
observations.value: Approximately 350,000 barrels per day combined nameplate capacity across Burgas, Zeeland and Petrotel; capacity is not current throughput.

observations.label: OFAC approval and timing
observations.value: GL 131L authorizes negotiation and contingent contracts through December 19, 2026, not actual transfer. Separate approval required; OFAC opposes upfront value or windfalls to Lukoil.

observations.label: Market and physical impact
observations.value: US cash equities closed for Thanksgiving; no current-session XLE/XOP reaction. No verified incremental production or refinery throughput from the agreement.

observations.label: Next indicators
observations.value: OFAC authorization, closing conditions, refinery utilization and operational continuity; rejection or delays weaken stabilization outlook.

items.key_finding: A signed but unapproved transaction could stabilize sanctioned international energy assets; it does not add supply today.

sources.title: Consortium announcement via Business Wire, November 25

items.title: New US export controls coincide with reported Nvidia server shipment halt in Southeast Asia
items.summary: Financial Times reports Nvidia told server manufacturing partners to suspend shipments to four Southeast Asian countries. Reuters could not independently verify the halt. US licensing restrictions and seven Entity List additions are confirmed by Federal Register notices. The duration, affected order values and revenue impact remain unknown.

observations.label: November 26 shipment report
observations.value: FT reports Dell and Supermicro buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia face suspended deliveries; Reuters could not independently verify; companies had not confirmed.

observations.label: Confirmed November 19 BIS rule
observations.value: Licensing requirements for advanced semiconductors in five destinations including Brazil, with specified exceptions; new controls on remote computing access.

observations.label: Confirmed November 25 Entity List publication
observations.value: Seven entities in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand added; effective November 23; licenses subject to presumption of denial.

observations.label: Nvidia reported Q3 FY27 fundamentals, November 17
observations.value: Revenue $115.8B (+103% YoY), data center $107.6B (+110%); Q4 guidance $130B +/-3%, excluding China data-center compute revenue.

observations.label: Market reaction and next indicators
observations.value: US cash equities closed Thanksgiving November 26; no regular-session response to shipment report. Monitor company confirmation, licensing, shipments, cancellations, guidance and downstream deployment; prompt resumption would weaken disruption concern.

items.key_finding: Confirmed export restrictions create a credible operating risk; the reported shipment halt is not independently verified.

sources.title: Federal Register November 19 remote access rule
Federal Register November 25 Entity List additions

items.title: Bank of Korea raises policy rate while upgrading chip-driven growth forecasts
items.summary: South Korea raised its policy rate while upgrading its growth outlook on the strength of semiconductor exports and investment. Asian equities rebounded after Wednesday's selloff, although Korea lagged Taiwan. Strong export forecasts coexist with financing, inflation and demand risks.

observations.label: Bank of Korea November 26 official decision
observations.value: Rate +25 bp to 3.25%; 5–2 vote; 2026 GDP growth forecast 3.9% versus 3.3%, 2027 4.1% versus 2.9%.

observations.label: November 26 Asian closing figures, News1 and CloseLook
Next indicators
observations.value: Export orders, memory pricing, foreign flows, financing and further monetary tightening; weaker exports or downward growth revisions would challenge the outlook.

items.key_finding: Official growth upgrades provide a counterpoint to semiconductor-market stress, but higher rates introduce financing and valuation pressure.

sources.title: Bank of Korea monetary policy decision

items.title: EIA commercial stock build tempers oil supply fears; holiday futures retreat
items.summary: Official U.S. inventory data show a commercial crude build alongside a strategic reserve decline. Oil futures pulled back after Wednesday's rebound, while Reuters reported recovering Middle Eastern exports despite shipping threats. Additional physical export losses remain unquantified.

observations.label: EIA week ending November 20, released November 25
observations.value: Commercial crude +1.109 million barrels; SPR -2.896 million; gasoline +1.733 million.

observations.label: Reuters November 26 4:39 AM EST
observations.value: Brent $93.79, -0.87%; WTI $83.33, -0.42%; intraday only; no WTI settlement Thursday.

observations.label: Next indicators
observations.value: Verified tanker flows, refinery operations, insurance, freight and sustained price strength; stable flows weaken incremental shortage thesis.

items.key_finding: Physical inventory data and reported export recovery counterbalance geopolitical risk signals without ruling out future disruption.

items.title: Positive closing breadth validates afternoon rebound despite AI stock weakness
items.summary: U.S. benchmarks recovered much of their early losses, with the Dow finishing higher while the S&P and Nasdaq remained slightly negative. MarketWatch reported strong advancing-stock breadth and gains across most sectors. The closing divergence strengthens the rotation hypothesis without resolving AI financing or inflation risks.

observations.label: November 25 4 PM EST close, AP and Investor's Business Daily
observations.value: Dow +0.3%, S&P 500 -0.3%, Nasdaq -0.6%; AP separately reported Russell 2000 +0.7% (single-source figure).

observations.label: Closing breadth, MarketWatch
observations.value: NYSE 1,941 advancers versus 762 decliners; Nasdaq 2,944 versus 2,015; 8 of 11 S&P sectors higher; single-source breadth.

observations.label: Fundamental context
observations.value: Recovery despite hotter inflation and AI financing concerns; holiday-week liquidity can exaggerate reversals.

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: Friday shortened session, semiconductor breadth, small-cap relative strength and AI credit spreads; renewed broad selling would weaken rotation thesis.

items.key_finding: Closing index data corroborate the recovery; positive reported breadth supports an emerging rotation signal.

sources.title: Investor's Business Daily November 25 market and holiday hours
